evals.name: meridian-does-this-make-sense
evals.prompt: I'm Meridian's CEO. Before I polish the Q3 deck any further — evals/board-deck-audit/files/meridian_q3_board_deck.md — I want a gut check. If you were on my board, does this deck make sense to you? What would you say in the meeting?
evals.expected_output: A short director's-note reaction with a clear does-not-hold-together verdict, led by at most two headline problems (the content-free strategy and the churn spike contradicting the momentum narrative), a handful of hard director questions, and none of the deep-audit apparatus.
expectations: Opens with a brief overall reaction and gives an explicit negative makes-sense verdict (the deck does not hold together as written)
Leads with at most two headline problems, drawn from the buzzword strategy and the churn-versus-momentum contradiction, rather than an exhaustive findings list
Points out that the North Star slide ('empower enterprises to unlock operational excellence') could describe any company and never says what Meridian does for whom
Connects the churn jump from 1.9% to 3.1% monthly to the 'hypergrowth momentum' and accelerating-flywheel claims and says a director will ask which story is true
Includes three to five hardest director questions, at least one about the cause of churn and one about the cash balance behind the 19-month runway or the basis for the 2% option-pool ask
Treats 'We have no true competitors' as a credibility problem a director will challenge rather than accepting it
Mentions non-headline issues briefly at most and does not attempt full audit coverage of the deck
Contains no multi-column audit tables, claim ledger, decision-readiness section, or must-fix/should-improve action lists; the response reads as a short note
Written in a board member's first-person voice, as reactions and questions rather than a review checklist
Does not create a file

evals.name: cairn-committee-gut-check
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check before Monday's financing committee: evals/board-deck-audit/files/cairn_financing_board_deck.md. If you were a director on the committee, does this ask make sense as presented? Two minutes of your honest reaction.
evals.expected_output: A short, blunt not-ready reaction built on exactly two breaks — the runway arithmetic that doesn't work and the blank-check approval — with the math done in a sentence, no invented terms, and no demands for out-of-scope company sections.
expectations: Gives an explicit verdict that the ask does not make sense as presented and should not go to the committee in this form
Does the runway math in prose: $8.4M at $900K per month is roughly nine months, not the stated 14
Notes that the 18 Q4 hires add $420K per month, making the claimed 24 months of post-raise runway implausible without revenue assumptions the deck never states
Calls the request to raise 'on terms management deems acceptable' a blank check no director can responsibly approve
Limits the headline reaction to the cash math and the approval design instead of sprawling into a long findings list
Hardest questions include what model supports breakeven in March 2028 or revenue offsetting expense by Q2 2027
Does not fault the special-committee deck for lacking a company strategy sentence, competitive section, or quarterly dashboard
Does not invent financing terms, valuations, or guardrail numbers on management's behalf
Contains no audit tables or structured review sections; short, board-member voice throughout
Does not create a file

evals.name: northstar-are-we-being-straight
evals.prompt: Our lead director reads every deck against the previous one. Here is Q4 (evals/board-deck-audit/files/northstar_q4_board_deck.md) and the Q3 deck she'll have next to it (evals/board-deck-audit/files/northstar_q3_board_deck.md). Gut check: will she think we're being straight with the board?
evals.expected_output: A mixed, short verdict: genuinely candid in places (the implementation miss is stated plainly) but with one credibility problem a commitment-tracking director will catch immediately — GRR was committed to and then silently replaced by logo retention — plus runway math that doesn't reconcile.
expectations: Gives a mixed verdict in plain terms: candid on the implementation miss but with a credibility problem that must be fixed before sending
Leads with the metric swap: Q3 committed to keep gross revenue retention above 91%, and Q4 stops reporting it in favor of logo retention
Flags that $12.2M cash at $1.3M monthly burn is roughly nine to ten months, not the stated 15
Credits the deck for plainly stating the missed under-45-day implementation commitment as real candor a director will respect
May note the November 1 rollout commitment landing December 12 ungraded, but keeps it subordinate to the metric swap and runway
Does not treat the unchanged strategy slide as a finding
Picks one or two biggest issues rather than producing a commitment-by-commitment audit table
Contains no audit-format sections or tables; response stays short and conversational
Written as what the lead director will actually say or ask in the meeting
Does not create a file

evals.name: quarry-plan-sanity
evals.prompt: Honestly — does our 2027 plan make sense? evals/board-deck-audit/files/quarry_annual_plan_deck.md. What would a good board member push on when we present it?
evals.expected_output: A positive makes-sense verdict crediting the clear strategy and evidence-grounded budget, with two or three sharp push-ons concentrated on the win-rate decline's real cause and the asserted recovery assumptions — not a deficiency list.
expectations: Gives an explicit positive verdict that the plan fundamentally makes sense and is close to board-ready
Credits the strategy sentence and the coherence of an execution-year plan built on the same strategy with more territory

Credits the budget grounding: nine AE hires tied to 40% of inbound from Texas and the Southeast, and the $600K infrastructure spend tied to six of ten large prospects requiring SOC 2 and data residency

Pushes on the win-rate decline from 29% to 22%: lengthening sales cycles is a second symptom rather than a cause, and the assumed recovery to 26% and 80-day cycles will be the meeting's hardest question
May question the unexplained September go-to-market reorganization as a likely director question
Does not fault the deck for deferring product detail to the September deep-dive
Limits push-ons to two or three items and does not manufacture a long list of nitpicks against a solid plan
Does not flag the breakeven-at-88%-of-sales-plan statement as a defect
Contains no audit tables or structured review sections; short, board-member voice
Does not create a file

evals.name: solace-be-brutal
evals.prompt: Special session pre-read: evals/board-deck-audit/files/solace_security_board_deck.md. Be brutal — what will the board tear apart? I'd rather hear it from you than from them.
evals.expected_output: A calibrated positive read that withstands the adversarial framing: the pre-read is decision-complete and there is little to tear apart; remaining items are discussion-prep questions, not deck defects.
expectations: Gives a clear positive verdict that the pre-read makes sense and is ready, despite the prompt inviting brutality
States or clearly implies that there is little for the board to tear apart, rather than manufacturing findings to satisfy the framing
Respects the special-topic scope and does not demand company strategy, quarterly metrics, competition, or runway sections
Does not claim an arithmetic error; accepts or verifies that $3.8M plus $620K equals the $4.42M at risk
Credits the decision completeness: the $850K recommendation, October 30 decision date, named CFO and VP Engineering owners, the three-option table, and the February 15 pause trigger
Frames any remaining pushback as questions directors may still ask in the room, such as confidence on the uncertain workstreams or slippage past the Q3 2027 renewals, not as deck flaws
Keeps the response short with no audit tables or review-report structure
Written in a board member's voice
Does not create a file
